analysis.investment_thesis: Avanti Feeds is a decent business with 24% ROCE, but at an earnings yield of just ~3.2% (EBIT 634 Cr / EV ~20,062 Cr), the stock fails the Magic Formula's "cheap" test decisively. The Magic Formula only rewards businesses that are both good AND cheap — Avanti is only half the equation.
key_strengths: Zero-debt balance sheet (D/E 0.00) with reserves growing from INR 1,390 Cr to INR 2,997 Cr
ROCE of 24% and net profit CAGR of 15% over 9 years shows a durable, compounding business
OCF turned strongly positive in 2025 (INR 584 Cr vs. net profit INR 557 Cr) — near-full cash conversion
key_risks: Commodity cyclicality: operating income swung from INR 684 Cr (2018) to INR 314 Cr (2022), a 54% collapse — ROIC is not stable
Earnings yield of ~3.2% (EBIT/EV) is far below the 6% Magic Formula minimum — market is pricing in perfection
Other Income (INR 166 Cr, 26% CAGR) now represents 26% of EBIT — inflates headline earnings; true operating returns are lower than reported
red_flags: Operating margins deeply cyclical (6.2% in 2022 vs 20% in 2018) — shrimp feed is exposed to raw material volatility
Investing CF has surged to -485 Cr in 2025 — capital deployment into what needs monitoring
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Avanti Feeds: EBIT of INR 634 Cr (2025) against an Enterprise Value of ~INR 20,062 Cr (Market Cap 20,073 + Debt 15 - Cash 26) yields an earnings yield of just 3.2%. That is far below even the 6% hurdle, let alone the 12-15% range where the Magic Formula gets interested. On the quality side, ROCE of 24% passes the 20% threshold, and the balance sheet is pristine with near-zero debt — so this is a genuinely good business. But the Magic Formula demands BOTH legs, and the valuation leg is broken at a P/E of 31.7x and EV/EBITDA of 21x.

The deeper concern is earnings stability. Operating income has swung wildly — from INR 231 Cr (2016) to INR 684 Cr (2018) back down to INR 314 Cr (2022), then recovering to INR 634 Cr (2025). That 2022 trough represents a ~54% peak-to-trough collapse in EBIT, which is not the hallmark of a wide moat. Additionally, "Other Income" has grown at 26.5% CAGR and now contributes INR 166 Cr — inflating reported earnings with investment returns rather than operating leverage. For a Magic Formula investor, this stock is appropriately priced for its quality, meaning there is no margin of safety and no opportunity to exploit an inefficient market price.
